hi everyone,

i am doing my undergraduate thesis on off axis replay of plankton holograms.

i'm using an argon laser, and as one of my experiments, have to see what efect changing the wavelength will have on the image i produce ( the aim of my thesis is to find the optimum replay scenario for these holograms). i have been asked to find out, why i can't replay the hologram with both wavelengths at once(488, and 514.5). i can't find any information on this on the web or in the books that i have. I THINK it's probably something blatently obvious. i appreciate any clarification you can provide

could it be something to do with one wavelength reaching the holographic plate early?

what adverse effect would this have on replay?

or is it something completely different?

thanks in advance folks,

andy

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Welcome u01anm3.

> could it be something to do with one wavelength reaching the holographic plate early?

No.

If it is a narrow band reflection hologram then the fringes will only reflect a narrow set of wavelengths, ie. a narrow band green reflection hologram will only reflect wavelengths 500nm - 530nm. Thus if the hologram is illuminated with 488nm the light simply passes through the hologram, not reflecting the image.

With broadband or full color holography film as long as both sets of fringes exist (those that reflect blue and green) then you could get a hologram with each wavelength.

For transmission holograms I think Kaveh's explaination and visuals are the best at explaining this. 

[http://www.holographer.org/articles/hg0 ... 00009.html](http://www.holographer.org/articles/hg00009/hg00009.html)
